newsitem.title: USA: ExFed Gov Gramley says Sept Fed rate move unlikely.
newsitem.headline: ExFed Gov Gramley says Sept Fed rate move unlikely.

text.p: Former Federal Reserve Board Governor Lyle Gramley said he sees less than an even chance the central bank will act on interest rates at its next policy meeting on September 24.

"I would say the chances are less than 50-50 that they will move this time unless we have something unexpectedly strong in terms of either increases in producer or consumer prices in August or in retail sales," Gramley said.
Gramley, a consulting economist at the Mortgage Bankers Association of America, told his views to Reuters in a telephone interview.

Gramley suggested a convincing case can be made from labor force figures released Friday and production and expenditure data that gross domestic product is moderating a "good bit" in the third quarter.
The economy generated 250,000 non-farm payroll jobs in August after creating a revised 228,000 in July. The jobless rate dipped to 5.1 percent -- a near 7-1/2-year low -- from 5.4 percent in July.
Yet Gramley said "when you dig below the surface" of the employment report, the figures are not as strong as they seem.
"The unemployment rate went down to 5.1, which is a big drop, but the main reason was we had a decline in the labor force, not a big increase in employment," Gramley said.

In short, the former Fed governor played downed the impact of the August jobs data. Referring to Fed policymakers, he said: "I doubt that anyone has changed their minds from where they were in August by these August employment data."

"If you thought there was no need to tighten on August 20, you probably won't think there is any need to on September 24," Gramley said. "Similarly, if you thought the economy was growing too fast on August 20, you probably haven't changed your mind on that."
